\section{Per-model absolute tables}
\label{app:absmaster}

Table~\ref{tab:master_abs_codellama7b} in the body is CodeLlama-7B, the model on which every arm exists. The same table for the other seven models follows; a cell that has not been evaluated renders as `--', and the mixture column exists only where a router gate has been trained.

% >>> GENERATED TABLE master_abs_codellama13b -- from tables/master_abs_codellama13b.tex; regenerate, then re-run inline_tables.py
% GENERATED 2026-09-14 15:51 UTC by scripts/analysis/59_master_tables.py

\begin{table*}[p]
\centering\scriptsize\setlength{\tabcolsep}{2pt}
\caption{\textbf{Every method against every obfuscation, CodeLlama-13B.} Raw accuracy (strict exact match), with \%\,\emph{b} after each system: its accuracy as a percentage of \texttt{base}'s on the same condition. \emph{base} is the untuned model; \emph{ICL} its one-shot prompt; \emph{clean LoRA} is tuned on unobfuscated code; \emph{breadth} on all five seen transforms; \emph{anchored} is the paired-consistency objective; \emph{family} is trained on the unseen family's sibling; \emph{mixture} is the learned-gate mixture of per-transform specialists; \emph{merge} is the DARE-TIES merge of them (keys in order: \texttt{base}, \texttt{base\_1shot}, \texttt{tuned\_L0}, \texttt{mono\_all}, \texttt{cons\_lam3}, \texttt{tuned\_X1}, \texttt{mole\_router}, \texttt{merge\_dare\_ties}). \textbf{The backward block is reported twice.} \emph{by execution} accepts any call that returns the gold value, and inversion is many-to-one, so a guess that lands on a common return value scores; \emph{by exact arguments} requires the gold call. Measured on CodeLlama-7B, 64--69\,\% of every system's backward successes are of the first kind, which is why the untuned model appears to read backwards almost as well as forwards. $\dagger$: format-failure rate above 0.25. `--': not run.}
